covers: skeletal animation on real-world models, Quaternius' Ultimate Modular Women: LoadModelAnimations from a file of its own (a 62-joint armature, 24 clips, no meshes), each Adventurer part and the sword loaded as its own model and checked against the animations (IsModelAnimationValid), and for Idle, Walk and Sword_Slash at whole, fractional and wrapped frames the body's bone matrices (UpdateModelAnimationBones) and each part's skinned vertices and normals (UpdateModelAnimation), a sample of them
notes: Whole frames match within 1.2e-6. Between frames, raylib 6.2's QuaternionSlerp keeps the first keyframe when its float dot product of the two reaches 1, and nlerps otherwise. helix-ray decides it by rounding its own keyframes (doubles) to floats, while raylib's are floats sampled in float arithmetic: on these slow clips (Idle; Walk wrapped) consecutive keyframes of 17 of 62 bones are within a float's ulp of one rotation, and the two decide them differently, so a bone held by one is interpolated by the other: up to 5.5e-4 in the bone matrices at fractional frames, which the bars carry. The poses themselves match within 6e-7.
